world.topic:
Start a world of your own, drive it, stop that drive yourself while it runs, and report what the world told you.

1. Write `child.json` with exactly this content:
   {"roles": [{"role": "paper-repo", "deliverables": ["at least one nonempty role artifact"]}, {"role": "internal-review-repo", "deliverables": ["at least one nonempty role artifact"]}], "edges": [["paper-repo", "internal-review-repo"]], "resources": [], "worker": {"agent": "claude-code", "model": "claude-sonnet-5-5", "max_executions": 6, "max_model_seconds": 300, "provider": {"base_url": "https://api.anthropic.com/v1", "credential_env": "ANTHROPIC_PROMO_API_KEY", "id": "anthropic", "protocol": "anthropic"}, "claude_code": {"env": {"CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL": "low"}}}}
2. Make the world: `ht-resource run worlds -- researchworld run --config child.json --topic "A three-section note on twin primes in report/report.md: each section drafted by paper-repo and reviewed by internal-review-repo before the next."` and wait for it to end; its output names the new world id.
3. Start driving it: `ht-resource run worlds -- researchworld execute <child world id> --loop`. Note the command reference it prints.
4. Right away, in the same turn and without waiting for the child world to make progress: as soon as `ht-resource status worlds` lists the drive as running, end it with `ht-resource stop worlds <reference>`.
5. Run `researchworld status <child world id>` and `ht-resource status worlds`.
6. Write `report/report.md`: the child world id, the drive's reference, the full answer of `ht-resource stop worlds` (or its full error), and from `researchworld status` whether the child world is still being driven and whether its container is running.
